_readme: Villas on Rio, 2111 Rio Grande Street, as js/slopes-apartments.js draws it. Rhode Partners, 2021: a 19-storey, 284-unit student tower whose north arm is roofed by one raking glass plane, wrapped in an L round the historic Kenney House, with a seven-storey wing at the south end and the pool on the tower roof. Metres in the footprint's oriented bounding box (js/westcampus.js obbOf): L=69.85, W=38.26, +u at bearing 185.1 deg - u=0 is the NORTH end on West 22nd Street and +u runs SOUTH; v=0 is the WEST edge on Rio Grande Street and +v runs EAST. Every number carries a _src naming a key in `sources`, or says derived or unknown. Read docs/apartments.md for the schema.
name: Villas on Rio

sources.S1: data/snapshots/2026-09-06/buildings.detailed.geojson feature e6abe8cf-5a15-4d11-9b04-f0a5c629d59a: name 'Villas on Rio', building_class 'apartments', num_floors null, final_height 9.6, source_height 'overture'. One ring, 13 vertices, 2087 m2, shaped like an L wrapped round a void at its north-west corner. The 9.6 m is OVERRIDDEN below and is wrong by 5.9x - see _heights_src; it is Overture's guess and predates the 2021 building.
sources.S2: Rhode Partners' own project page, rhodepartners.com/student-housing-villas-on-rio, read 2026-09-06: 'this 352,000-square-foot residential tower spans 19 floors containing 284 units housing 1,155 beds. The design thoughtfully integrates a historic Victorian structure on the property. The building features an ANGLED GLASS FACADE responding to local setback regulations, with CUSTOM-FORMED EXTERIOR PANELS that establish angular design motifs repeated throughout interior spaces.' Rhode Partners is the architect; completed 2021.
sources.S3: SkyscraperPage's Austin thread title for the building, 'Villas on Rio | 185 Feet | 19 Floors | COMPLETE' (skyscraperpage.com/forum/showthread.php?t=235408), with apartmentfinder and apartments.com listings agreeing on 19 stories, 2021, 2111 Rio Grande St. 185 ft = 56.39 m, which is the parapet height used here.
sources.S4: rambleratx.com's West Campus review of the building, read 2026-09-06: 19 storeys, 2021, 856 beds, 'wraps in an L-shape around the historic Kenney House', which is now a Starbucks, and a four-level parking garage under the main structure. The Kenney House is snapshot feature 4fe52d88-e63b-49d8-8032-350db80c3b50, 'Kenney Lomax House', 2 floors, 10.9 m, whose centroid lands at (u 11.5, v 13.5) in this file's frame - the void in the ring's north-west corner IS that house, and the ring is the L round it.
sources.S5: The architect's own photographs, downloaded 2026-09-06 from the S2 page and from villasonrio.com (the operator's site) into the session scratchpad next/build/villas-on-rio/ref/: src_00 and src_08 are aerials from the north-west looking south-east, src_07 a street-level dusk photograph of the north-west corner, src_09 a drone nadir of the roof pool, src_01 an interior against the raking glass, src_10 the roof deck at dusk. They are copyrighted and are NOT committed; every number read off them is written down here instead.
sources.S6: Google Earth 3D, imagery 12/3/2023, captured 2026-09-06 with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on hardware GL and page.screenshot(): a NADIR at 420 m over the centroid. It was VERIFIED before anything was read off it - the snapshot ring projected on to it at the scale bar's 0.2353 m/px about the canvas centre lands on the roof edges on all four sides (ref/earth/nadir_overlay.png). The nadir was then resampled into this file's (u, v) frame at 10 px/m with a 5 m grid (ref/plan_grid.png), and every plan dimension below - the pool, the raking glass's extent, the roof step at u 45.5 - was read in metres off that gridded plan. The four Earth obliques taken in the same run were DISCARDED: the camera had not settled at the URL's look-at (its own readout put it 140 m off) and the mesh over this block is soft. S5's photographs are the elevation source instead.
sources.S7: data/roads.geojson: West 22nd Street runs east-west 43 m north of the centroid, Rio Grande Street north-south 28 m west of it, West 21st Street 83 m south, Nueces Street 69 m east. The footprint's u=0 edge is 37.7 m north of the centroid, so it stands on W 22nd; v=0 is 19 m west of it, so it fronts Rio Grande. That is what fixes which end is which: u=0 NORTH on W 22nd, +u runs SOUTH; v=0 WEST on Rio Grande, +v runs EAST. 21 Rio (snapshot 73c958f3, 21 floors, 73.5 m) stands 60 m due south and is the tower standing behind the building in S5's aerials, which is the second check on the same reading.
sources.derived: a number computed from the ones above and marked so; 'unknown' stays unknown.

footprint._src: S1 verbatim. The ring is worth keeping vertex for vertex: the big void at its north-west corner is the Kenney House (S4), and the two notches at u 41.5-48.7 are a light well and a slot the building wraps at its south-east.

_frame_src: obbOf(ring) as the generator computes it (M_LAT 110540, mLon 111320 cos lat): L=69.85, W=38.26, +u at bearing 185.10 deg, +v at 95.10. Which end is which street is S7, not a guess.

levels._src: DERIVED from two stated numbers and one proportion: 19 floors (S2, S3, S4) inside 185 ft = 56.39 m to the parapet (S3). The parapet is 1.4 m, so the roof deck is 55.0. The ground floor is 4.6 m - on S5 src_00's crop ref/c00_taupe3.jpg the storefront is about 1.6 times a residential floor - which leaves 50.4 m for the other 18, i.e. 2.80 m floor to floor. 2.80 is tight and it is meant to be: this is a 1,155-bed pod building on 284 units (S2). Uncertainty about 0.1 m a floor. The floor lines here are 0 and 4.6 + k x 2.8 for k = 0..17.
levels._heights_src: THIS OVERRIDES the snapshot's 9.6 m (S1), which is Overture's guess for a building it never saw - the tower was completed in 2021 and the guess is 5.9x short. 56.4 m comes from S3's 185 ft, which agrees with 19 floors at the pitch above. The wing's 21.4 m is 7 storeys counted on S5 src_00. The rake's 24.2 m eave is the ninth floor line, read off S5 src_00 against the wing's parapet in the same frame.

colours._src: Sampled from S5's src_00 by median-cut clustering of patches of one material, not by eye. src_00 is a clear-day aerial from the north-west at midday: the WEST face is in sun and the NORTH face in shade, so every value below cites the sunlit patch where one exists and says so where it does not. The day hex is entered; golden and night come from js/westcampus.js's ramp(), as every other file here does it.

precast._src: S5 src_00 (1560-1700, 640-760), a patch of the sunlit west face: the seven clusters are #edefef, #e6e9eb, #e0e4e6, #dae1e4, #d7dde0, #cad2d6 and #6b7a7f. The first five are one material under slightly different shading - the white glass-fibre-reinforced-concrete panel - and #e8ebec is their middle. The panels are faceted, which is why one material gives five clusters.

recess._src: S5 src_00, the same patch: the darkest cluster, 19 % of it, which is the dark rectangle in every panel. In shade (src_00 900-1150, 750-1000) the same rectangle reads #233439, so this is the sunlit value.

glassPale._src: S5 src_00, the pale mint units seen right across both faces; the #cad2d6 cluster in the tight patch is this glass in sun, entered a step greener because that cluster is half white surround. The windows range from mint to grey with the sky; one tone is entered.

rakeGlass._src: S5 src_00 (760-900, 420-560) and (880-1000, 300-420), two patches of the raking glass plane: clusters #234b5e, #3d6578, #355e74 and #254d63. Entered between them. A deep teal-blue - a big plane of insulated vision glass seen against the sky, and the darkest thing on the building.

rakeGlassA._src: the darkest of the four. S5 src_00 (760-900, 420-560) and (880-1000, 300-420), the two patches of the raking glass: this is that cluster, entered on its own. The four clusters were averaged into `rakeGlass` while the plane was twenty stair-steps and could carry only one tone; the plane can carry all four now, one per pane (`fields` with `fieldRule: checker` on rakeGlassSkin), which is what a wall of insulated vision glass does - every pane returns a different piece of sky. S6's Google Earth (imagery 12/3/2023), re-flown 2026-09-08 at a camera matched to this app's own aerial pose over the north-west corner, shows the same thing and is the reason the flat tone was not left alone: mint panes beside slate ones, in patches, not a field.

rakeGlassB._src: the lightest of the four. S5 src_00 (760-900, 420-560) and (880-1000, 300-420), the two patches of the raking glass: this is that cluster, entered on its own. The four clusters were averaged into `rakeGlass` while the plane was twenty stair-steps and could carry only one tone; the plane can carry all four now, one per pane (`fields` with `fieldRule: checker` on rakeGlassSkin), which is what a wall of insulated vision glass does - every pane returns a different piece of sky. rakeGlassC._src: the third. S5 src_00 (760-900, 420-560) and (880-1000, 300-420), the two patches of the raking glass: this is that cluster, entered on its own. The four clusters were averaged into `rakeGlass` while the plane was twenty stair-steps and could carry only one tone; the plane can carry all four now, one per pane (`fields` with `fieldRule: checker` on rakeGlassSkin), which is what a wall of insulated vision glass does - every pane returns a different piece of sky. rakeGlassD._src: the second-darkest. S5 src_00 (760-900, 420-560) and (880-1000, 300-420), the two patches of the raking glass: this is that cluster, entered on its own. The four clusters were averaged into `rakeGlass` while the plane was twenty stair-steps and could carry only one tone; the plane can carry all four now, one per pane (`fields` with `fieldRule: checker` on rakeGlassSkin), which is what a wall of insulated vision glass does - every pane returns a different piece of sky. S6's Google Earth (imagery 12/3/2023), re-flown 2026-09-08 at a camera matched to this app's own aerial pose over the north-west corner, shows the same thing and is the reason the flat tone was not left alone: mint panes beside slate ones, in patches, not a field.

taupe._src: S5 src_00 (1500-1800, 1080-1300), the seven-storey wing: clusters #a6a19d, #afa9a4 and #b8b1aa are one material - a warm grey precast - and #b0aaa4 is their middle. #d1d5d3 in the same patch is the white window surround (trimWhite) and #383c38 the openings.

trimWhite._src: S5 src_00, the #d1d5d3 cluster from the taupe patch: the 0.14 m white surround round every opening in the wing, lifted a little because that cluster is half shadowed reveal.

glassCurtain._src: derived from rakeGlass: the curtain wall on the wedge's north end and at the glazed north-west corner is the same glass as the rake in S5 src_07, seen more nearly face-on, so it is entered one step lighter and greyer.

mull._src: S5 src_07: the curtain wall's mullions read as light anodised aluminium against the glass.

storeGlass._src: S5 src_00 (1450-1700, 1330-1420), the ground-floor storefront under the wing: clusters #29251b and #655b50 are the shop interiors in shadow behind the glass. Entered as a dark neutral - a deep shopfront in shade.

baseDark._src: S5 src_00, the same patch's #5e584c: the soffit and the recessed wall behind the ground-floor columns, and the service bay at the wing's south end.

baseConc._src: S5 src_00 (1330-1450, 1300-1400): the exposed concrete columns on the storefront line read #d5c8bd in sun and #968b7b in shade; entered between.

coping._src: derived: the parapet capping, entered as the precast a shade cooler, which is what the roof edges read as in S6's nadir.

colours._roofMem_src: S6's nadir: the membrane roof over the wing and the tower reads a light warm grey with the condenser fields dark on it. Golden and night entered the way the other files here enter a top face.
colours._condenser_src: S6's nadir: split-system condensers in rows over both roofs; entered between their sunlit tops and their own shadow, as 2706 Rio Grande's file does.

poolWater._src: S5 src_09, the drone nadir of the roof pool: the water is a strong tropical teal. Read off that photograph, not lifted.

deckTile._src: S5 src_09: the warm sand-coloured tile deck round the pool and the timber platform at its west end.

spaTile._src: S5 src_09: the smaller square spa at the pool's west end, a lighter tile.

railGlass._src: S5 src_09 and src_10: the frameless glass balustrade round the roof deck.

mech._src: S6's nadir: the mechanical penthouse and stair overrun on the tower roof, a pale grey box.

sign._src: S5 src_00: VILLAS ON RIO on the wing's west wall is dark charcoal lettering on the taupe.

pergola._src: S5 src_00 and src_10: the white steel trellis over the roof deck's lounge.

skins._src: Two wall rules and two glass rules. The white tower and the wedge wear `panel`; the seven-storey wing wears `taupeGrid`; the ground floor wears `store`; the wedge's north end and the glazed north-west corner wear `curtain`. Nothing else was photographed differently.

panel._src: S2's 'custom-formed exterior panels', COUNTED on S5 src_00 (ref/c00_white.jpg) 2026-09-08, on the sunlit west face, patch x 655-845 y 210-610. Twenty-five openings in seven rows were found by connected components under luminance 200. THE ROWS: tops at y 4, 64, 123, 182, 241, 299, 356, so the row pitch is (356-4)/6 = 58.7 px, and this file's storey is 2.80 m, which fixes the vertical scale at 20.95 px/m. THE COLUMNS: within a row the left edges are 24, 72, 120, 165 - centre to centre 47.5 px - and every second row is 24 px along, exactly half of that, seven rows running without a miss. THE OPENING: 34-36 px tall = 1.62-1.72 m, so 1.65; and a horizontal cut at each row's own mid-height puts the not-white run at 0.51-0.57 of the column pitch, so 1.70 m of the 3.15. Shares check it: 24.1 % of the patch is below luminance 200 and 26.4 % below 210, against the 31.8 % a 1.70 x 1.65 opening fills of a 3.15 x 2.80 cell - the difference is the glass that returns sky and reads brighter than 210 - and 69.3 % of the patch is above 240, which is the white panel itself. THE PITCH IS 3.15 m, not the 1.575 this file carried: the 1.575 came from a luminance profile of ref/earth2/w.png that summed TWO storey bands (rows y 292-306 AND y 345-358) which are offset half a pitch from each other, so the sum shows a centre every half pitch; that same note recorded 'the occasional 44 and 48 [px]' and called them a skipped column, and they are the true single-row pitch. The 3.20 m this file first had and then withdrew was right. THE OPENING'S PARTS: S5 src_07 (ref/c07_panels.jpg) shows each opening is a pale mint glass slot BESIDE a dark panel, and the hand changes bay to bay. This generator has no per-bay hand, so the DARK is kept whole and centred - the pane itself, 1.00 m of `recess` - and the mint is split to either side of it as a `frame` with h 0, two 0.35 m bars and nothing above or below, which is the exact average of the two hands. It has to be that way round and not the other: with the dark split into two bars round a mint centre the opening stops reading as one window and reads as a pair of slats, which is what the first render of this fix showed at the sidewalk camera. That gives 1.00 x 1.65 m of dark (18.7 % of the wall) and 0.70 x 1.65 m of mint (13.1 %), against the 15 % and 9-13 % the patch's own histogram puts in the recess and glassPale bands. The 0.70 m sill is derived: 1.15 m of white lies between one row's foot and the next row's head (58.7 - 35 px), and it is split 0.70 below the opening and 0.45 above, which is where a sill and a head sit on a 2.80 m floor. NO CHECKER. `fields: [recess, precast]` with `fieldRule: checker` was here and drew the row stagger, but in this generator the opening under that rule IS the leftover field rectangle, and a `bays` skin's `window` takes no field rule - so the glass slot was drawn in the blank bays as well, and the wall carried two different marks at once: a 0.955 x 1.50 m dark rectangle in half the bays and a 0.50 x 0.90 m pale slot in the other half, each moving a module every storey. A blind reader shown the frames named it twice unprompted - sizes vary from tall slots to tiny squares, they do not line up into floors, you cannot count storeys anywhere. One opening per bay on the measured 3.15 m pitch is drawn instead; the stagger is in `todo` with the one generator key that would bring it back.

taupeGrid._src: S5 src_00 (the crop ref/c00_taupe3.jpg): the seven-storey wing is a warm grey precast wall with single portrait windows on a tight module, each in a crisp white surround about 0.14 m wide - a different rule from the tower's panels, and the surrounds are the thing that reads at any distance. Six window rows above the storefront were counted on that crop, which is where the wing's seven storeys come from. The bay is 1.43 m: the SEVENTEEN columns that same crop shows across the wing's 24.35 m west face, which is what 24.35/17 comes to. It was entered as 2.30 m before - a number that contradicts its own count, and would have put ten columns there - and a luminance profile of the wing in ref/earth2/w.png (rows y 530-542) gives gaps of 18.5-22.5 px against 13.65 px/m, i.e. 1.4-1.6 m, which is the same module.

curtain._src: S5 src_07: a stick curtain wall on about a 1.5 m mullion module with a horizontal at every floor - the glazed north end of the wedge over the entrance at 2111, and the full-height glazed corner where the tower's north and west faces meet. No `window` key: the whole field is glass and the strips are the mullions.

store._src: S5 src_00 (ref/c00_taupe3.jpg): the ground floor on Rio Grande is a continuous glazed storefront on about a 1.6 m mullion module with a transom high in the opening, set back under the wall above on square exposed-concrete columns. The 4.6 m ground floor is derived - it is plainly taller than a residential floor in that crop, about 1.6 times - and 4.6 is what closes 19 floors on to the 185 ft of S3.

base._src: the unphotographed ground floor: the east and south sides face a surface car park and the neighbour, and wear the plainest thing the building has - the dark base the storefront's fascia is made of.

rakeGlassSkin._fields_src: the four glass clusters S5 src_00 gives for this plane, one per pane, indexed by bay + storey so the patchwork runs diagonally rather than in stripes. `field` stays their median for anything that asks for a single tone.
rakeGlassSkin._floorLine_src: S5 src_07: this is the same stick system as the `curtain` skin, which carries a 0.16 m horizontal at every floor. On a plumb wall that is a `louvre` at the 2.80 m storey pitch; on the plane the floor lines land where those heights CUT it - 3.38 m apart up the slope at 56.0 deg - so it is `floorLine`, which takes the building's own levels, and not a pitch that would have been wrong by 21 %.
rakeGlassSkin._src: S5 src_00 and src_08: the raking plane is one field of deep teal insulated glass on a light mullion grid at about 1.55 m, the same module as the `curtain` skin's. It is ONE plane now (see the `rake` block), so the 1.55 m module is 1.55 m measured on the glass and the reveal is normal to it; it used to wear the risers of a twenty-step stair. No `window` key - the whole field is glass.

blocks._src: The north arm on West 22nd Street below the rake's eave, in ONE block so its west and east elevations are one wall each on the panel rule's own 1.575 m bay. u 0-20.74, v 22.51-37.42 off S6's rectified nadir (the arm is the part of the ring east of the Kenney House's void); its top at the eave, 24.2 m.

u0._src: S5 src_07: the arm's north end on West 22nd Street is a full-height curtain wall, with the entrance, the address 2111 and the VILLAS ON RIO sign under it. It is where the raking glass comes down to the ground, and the two read as one glazed corner.

blocks._src: THE RAKING GLASS PLANE, one surface. S2 calls it the 'angled glass facade responding to local setback regulations' and it is the whole north end of the building. Its FOOT is the u0 edge (the north end on West 22nd Street) at the ninth floor line, 24.2 m, read off S5 src_00 against the wing's parapet in the same frame; its HEAD is that same edge 20.74 m south at 54.95 m, the roof deck. run 20.74, rise 30.75, pitch 56.0 deg. Both ends come off S6's rectified nadir (the arm's own depth) and S5 src_00's elevation, and they are the same two numbers the twenty stair-steps this replaces were cut from - 20 x 1.037 m of run and 20 x 1.538 m of rise. The generator drew a stair because it had no sloped wall; `rake` is that wall, so the treads and risers are gone and the silhouette is one straight line. The flanks are the building's own `panel` rule, clipped to the wedge, which is why `panelSliver` and `panelSliverBlank` are gone with them.
blocks._rake_src: `face: u0` leans the north edge; `run` is omitted so it is the plan's whole depth behind that edge, 20.74 m - a pure wedge, which is what this building is. The plane's own numbers read back from slopesApartments.built[i].rakes.

u0._src: the leaning face itself: one field of deep teal glass on its 1.55 m mullion module, tiled in metres ALONG the slope, so the module is 1.55 m ON THE GLASS as it is on the building.

blocks._src: The 19-storey mass, S2 and S3. Its south end is at u 45.5: S6's nadir has a clean parapet line right across the plan there, with the pool and the tower's own roof north of it and a dense condenser field south of it, and S5's aerials show the taupe wing starting at that same point in the elevation. The west and east edges are the ring's own, v 0 and v 37.42.

u1._src: the south face shows only above the seven-storey wing that stands against it.

v1._src: the east face looks at a surface car park and was never photographed; it wears the panel rule with the plain dark base under it instead of a storefront.

overrides._src: S5 src_00 (ref/sample_marks.jpg) and src_07: the building's north-west corner is glazed for its full height - a vertical glass slot about 4.5 m on each return, where the north face over the Kenney House meets the west face on Rio Grande. One region catches both walls, because an override takes the part of ANY axis-parallel wall inside it.

blocks._parapet_src: 1.4 m of upstand right round the roof deck, which puts the top at 56.4 m = 185 ft (S3). S5 src_00 shows a clean lip above the wall on every side, with the pool deck's glass balustrade standing inside it.

roofItems._src: S6's nadir: the mechanical penthouse and stair overrun fill the middle of the tower roof east of the pool deck; the height is derived from a plant room's usual storey.
S6's nadir: condenser rows along the tower roof's east edge. Seven by two counts the visible clusters, not the units.

blocks._src: The seven-storey taupe wing at the south end, u 45.5 to the ring's 69.85, full plan depth. Six window rows above the storefront were counted on S5 src_00 (ref/c00_taupe3.jpg), so 7 storeys and a roof deck at 21.4 m, which IS the top of floor 7 on this file's floor lines.

v0._src: the west face on Rio Grande: S5 src_00's crop ref/c00_taupe3.jpg has the storefront set back about 1.7 m behind the wall above on square concrete columns roughly 6.6 m apart, and VILLAS ON RIO in dark letters high on the taupe at the north end of that face, above the entry. The letter size is read off the same crop against the 2.8 m floor.

v1._src: the east face on the car park, unphotographed: the same wall rule with the plain dark base.

u1._src: the south face stands about 8 m from the neighbour and no photograph reaches it; the same rule again.

blocks._parapet_src: S5 src_00: a clean lip round the wing's roof on the three free sides; none on the north edge, where the tower stands on it.

roofItems._src: S6's nadir: the wing's roof is the densest condenser field on the site - one or two units a flat, right across it. Nine by four counts the visible clusters.
S6's nadir: the stair and lift overrun standing above the wing's roof, near its middle.

deck._src: The roof pool deck at the tower's north-west corner, read off S6's rectified nadir (ref/plan_grid.png) and checked against S5 src_09, a drone nadir of the same deck: a long pool with a square spa at its west end, a tile deck round it, and a frameless glass balustrade on the Rio Grande edge with a white steel trellis over the lounge. S4 and the operator's site both call it a rooftop pool with hot tub and cabanas.

items._src: the tile deck, u 22.4-42.2 v 1.9-11.6 off the gridded plan
the main pool, 12.0 x 5.0 m off the gridded plan; src_09 shows depth markings along its long side
the square spa at the pool's west end, raised on its own coping (src_09)
the frameless glass balustrade on the Rio Grande edge of the deck (src_09, src_10)
the white steel trellis over the lounge at the deck's north end (src_00, src_10); a trellis of rafters is beyond the generator, so this is its top plate on four posts

todo: THE HALF-MODULE ROW STAGGER IS NOT DRAWN, and it is the only thing about this wall that is measured and missing. S5 src_00 is unambiguous: within a row the openings are 3.15 m centre to centre, and every second row is offset 1.575 m - exactly half - for seven rows without a miss, which is S2's 'angular design motifs'. This file draws the right pitch, the right opening and the right rows, in plumb columns. It cannot draw the offset: the stagger needs a rule that skips a bay by (bay + storey) parity, and a `bays` skin's `window` has no such rule. `fields` with `fieldRule: checker` HAS one, which is why the previous round used it, but under that rule the opening is the leftover field rectangle and the `window` is drawn on every bay regardless - see `panel`'s _src for what that looked like. One key ends it: `windowRule: 'checker'` beside `fieldRule` in windowsFromBays, skipping the window where (ci + storey) is odd. Then `bay` halves to 1.575, the opening stays 1.70 wide - wider than its own bay, which the tiler already allows - and nothing else in this file moves.

The window cannot be dropped in favour of a field rectangle, and this is why: it is the only thing on this building that lights at night. Every `bays` window carries a `lit` flag and a night tone; a field rectangle carries neither. Rendered at time-of-day 1.0 the tower is read entirely by its lit windows - remove them and nineteen storeys go black beside a lit Torre and a lit Signature 1909.

The custom-formed panels crease diagonally - that is S2's 'angular design motifs' and it is the first thing you see in S5 src_07. Every crease is a fold of about 20-40 mm across a 3.2 x 2.8 m panel, so it is under a pixel at the oblique camera and about half a pixel at walking height; it is not drawn, and this file does not pretend it is. If it is ever wanted it is one diagonal quad per panel, not a skin change.

The two notches in the ring at u 41.5-48.7 (a 3.9 x 5.1 m light well and a 3.3 x 18.4 m slot open to the east) are in the footprint but not in the massing: the tower and the wing are given as rectangles that meet at u 45.5, so the notches are filled. They are about 3 m wide and face a car park; a plan polygon per block would draw them.

The wedge's east flank (v 37.42) and the tower's and the wing's east and south faces were never photographed - the car park side and the neighbour's wall block every angle - and they wear the same rule as the faces that were.

The four-level parking garage under the building (S4) is not drawn: no photograph reaches its screen and S6's nadir cannot see it. The ground floor is a storefront right round the west side instead, which is what S5 src_00 shows there.

_rake._src: The raking glass plane, ONE surface, as the `rake` block draws it: foot on the u0 edge at 24.2 m, head 20.74 m south at 54.95 m, so run 20.74, rise 30.75, pitch atan(30.75/20.74) = 56.0 deg and a slope length of 37.091 m. It was twenty blocks of 1.037 m run and 1.538 m rise until the generator gained a sloped wall; those steps stood ON this line, which is why the two silhouettes are the same line and only the sawtooth has gone. Read back at runtime from slopesApartments.built[i].rakes as { block: 'rake', face: 'u0', pitch, run, rise, len } - the numbers here are what that must report.
